item.title: Anambra home to political icons like Zik, Ekwueme, Soludo – Shettima
item.description: By Nwabueze Okonkwo ONITSHA – Vice-President Kashim Shettima has described Anambra State as a home of accomplished political leaders, citing Nigeria’s first President, Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe; former Vice-President, Dr. Alex Ekwueme; and the incumbent governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo. Shettima made the observation on Thursday at a joint mega rally organised by the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) and the All Progressives Congress (APC) under the banner of Progressives Working Together. The Vice-President, who represented President Bola Tinubu at the rally, said he was not surprised that Soludo had embraced what he described as the visionary politics of national unity associated with Azikiwe and Ekwueme. He commended the governor for what he described as his courage and political approach in the current political dispensation. Shettima also assured Nigerians, particularly residents of Anambra State, that Tinubu’s administration would reposition the country if given another term in 2027. In his remarks, Soludo said APGA and APC had unanimously endorsed Tinubu for a second term in office. As part of the alliance, the governor handed over the APGA flag to the APC, describing the move as a demonstration of the parties’ commitment to working together. Soludo further disclosed that elected APGA members in the state and National Assemblies would work with their APC counterparts in their respective legislative caucuses. He said the arrangement was aimed at promoting cooperation, national unity and the indivisibility of Nigeria. item.title: Kwara South: APC candidate Adewoye confident of victory
item.description: By Demola Akinyemi, Ilorin The All Progressives Congress (APC) senatorial candidate for Kwara South in the 2027 general election, Prince Olalekan Adewoye, has expressed confidence in his ability to represent the people of the district effectively, saying his business experience and grassroots interventions have prepared him for public service. Adewoye said his conviction was anchored on more than three decades of experience in business, philanthropic activities and commitment to grassroots development. Speaking in an interview with journalists, the industrialist said he was passionate about translating his private-sector experience into public service, despite not having previously held an elective position or served as a political appointee. Addressing concerns about his lack of political experience and the challenge posed by established opposition politicians, Adewoye said he was confident of earning the support of voters. “I am convinced of my capacity and believe I have what it takes to represent the people effectively,” he said. He argued that voters should assess candidates based on their records, capacity and acceptability rather than previous political positions alone. According to him, his years in business have equipped him with the ability to manage people from different backgrounds, create value and deploy resources efficiently. He said these skills would be useful in legislative representation, particularly in ensuring that public resources and government programmes deliver tangible benefits to constituents. Adewoye disclosed that before joining the senatorial race, he had been involved in philanthropic activities through a foundation established to address some of the social and economic challenges facing residents of Kwara South. He identified healthcare, education and support for small businesses as critical areas requiring attention in the district. He said the foundation had provided equipment to individuals seeking to establish or expand businesses, supported healthcare interventions, including health insurance for elderly people, and assisted artisans and other vulnerable groups. According to him, the interventions were designed to promote self-reliance and economic independence rather than encourage beneficiaries to depend on periodic handouts. “We should not simply tell young people to look for jobs. We must help them acquire the skills, resources and support they need to create value,” he said. The APC candidate said his proposed representation would prioritise expanding economic opportunities for young people, traders, artisans and small business operators. He also disclosed plans to establish a trust fund to bring together individuals and organisations willing to support entrepreneurs and other deserving residents of Kwara South. item.title: Sanwo-Olu gives LASUED best graduate N5m, job
item.description: By Elizabeth Osayande Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, has rewarded the overall best graduating student of the Lagos State University of Education (LASUED), Blessed Mercy Olawunmi, with N5 million and automatic employment. The award was announced on Thursday, November 19, during the institution’s maiden convocation ceremony held at its Oto/Ijanikin campus. Olawunmi, of the Department of Home Economics, College of Vocational and Entrepreneurship Education, emerged top of the pioneering graduating class of 2,486 students, including 84 first-class graduates, with a Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA) of 4.98. Sanwo-Olu also announced a cash reward of N2.5 million each for the best graduating students from the university’s seven colleges. Apart from the governor’s award, Olawunmi received N250,000 and a commemorative plaque from the university, while Oto-Awori Local Government presented her with N1 million. The council chairman, Kareem Azeez Abiodun, also announced a reward of N500,000 each for the other best graduating students from the colleges. Speaking at the ceremony, the Vice-Chancellor, Prof. Bidemi Bilkis Lafiaji-Okuneye, thanked Sanwo-Olu for assenting to the law establishing the university in 2022. She also commended the Governing Council, staff, students and other stakeholders for their contributions towards making the institution a source of pride. However, she appealed to the governor to intervene in four areas requiring urgent attention: construction of a podcast and photojournalism studio, reconstruction of the perimeter fence, reclamation of swampy land at the main campus and completion of the 750-seat auditoriums at the Epe and Ijanikin campuses. The Vice-Chancellor disclosed that more than 60 per cent of the main campus land was swampy, leaving the institution with limited space for expansion. She said the university currently occupied only the dry portions of the land and was becoming increasingly cramped, adding that reclamation would provide room for future development. She noted that a female hostel being constructed by the Tertiary Education Trust Fund (TETFund) was already located on the site. “Your Excellency, sir, these four appeals are strategic investments rather than isolated requests. A studio will enrich what we teach. Secure fencing will protect people who teach — our land. Reclaimed land will create room for all that we still hope to build. An auditorium will provide a gathering space in which scholarship, professional development, and public engagement can flourish,” she said. Lafiaji-Okuneye also appreciated the Governing Council for its guidance and oversight, the Ministry of Tertiary Education for facilitating the university’s requests to the governor, and staff for sustaining the institution through its transition. item.title: Fubara inspects beach road, woos investors to Rivers
item.description: By Daniel Abia, Port Harcourt Rivers State Governor, Siminalayi Fubara, has expressed satisfaction with the progress of work on the Ngo-Atlantic Oyorokoto Beach Road in Andoni Local Government Area, urging prospective investors to explore the area’s tourism potential. Fubara gave the assurance on Thursday during an inspection of the project, promising that the access road to the beach would be asphalted before December and ahead of the next Tourists Beach Party. Speaking with journalists after the inspection, the governor said he visited the project site to assess the level of work, recalling that his administration had created an official access road to the beach before the declaration of a state of emergency in Rivers State. He said the project experienced some delays during the period but that the state government had since resumed meeting its obligations to contractors to ensure the development of the area into a tourism destination. “We’ve been following up and meeting our own side of the obligation to ensure that one of the promises that we made to our people that day — that we want to make this place a tourist centre — comes to reality. And that is one of the main reasons we came here to see what is happening and the extent of the job that has been done,” he said. Fubara described the inspection as an opportunity to assess first-hand the progress made on the project. He said work on the beach access road was largely satisfactory, adding that the major outstanding task was the asphalting of the road, which he assured would be completed before December or ahead of the next Tourists Beach Party. The governor also disclosed that he inspected the other section of the road leading to the fishing ports, where he said only a culvert, measuring about 100 metres from the fishing centre, remained to be completed. Fubara said the level of work recorded was significantly better than what was previously on ground. He urged prospective investors to take advantage of the area’s tourism and commercial opportunities, assuring them that they had nothing to fear about investing in Rivers State. item.title: 2027: Tinubu Doesn’t Need To Rig Any Election, He’ll Win Because He’s Done Well — Soludo
item.description: Anambra State Governor, Charles Soludo, has declared that President Bola Tinubu does not need to manipulate the 2027 presidential election to secure re-election, insisting that his performance in office will earn him victory. Soludo said the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential ticket of Tinubu and Vice President Kashim Shettima was already in a strong position ahead of the election, arguing that no opposition candidate had presented a credible alternative to the ruling party. The governor spoke on Thursday at a 2027 presidential campaign rally in Anambra State attended by Shettima, Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council Abdul’aziz Yari, former Anambra State governor Chris Ngige and Imo State Governor Hope Uzodimma, among other party chieftains. “To our people, this election, to the best of our knowledge, is already won and lost. The President doesn’t need to rig the election. President Tinubu doesn’t need to rig the election “All over the country today, in every state of Nigeria, it is President Tinubu and Shetima’s ticket versus one other party. Whereas you have some other candidates who are strong in some parts of the country but don’t exist in others. “If you then take the totality of it all, do the arithmetic. This election is literally over. President Tinubu and Shettima, they are doing very well. They will win because they have done well,” he added. ﻿ Soludo also praised the Tinubu administration’s economic policies, security efforts and social intervention programmes, describing its agenda as superior to those presented by previous presidential candidates. “We know that there is still work to be done. And that work to be done means moving now from stability, having rescued the economy from total collapse, now moving into the next phase of shared prosperity. But let’s not kid ourselves. You don’t change a winning team. The Tinubu-Shetima ticket is the winning team,” the governor said. 2027 Presidential Election COMBO: Peter Obi, Atiku Abubakar, Bola Tinubu and Omoyele Sowore The 2027 presidential election, which is less than 60 days away, is expected to feature several prominent political figures, including Tinubu of the APC, Atiku Abubakar of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Peter Obi of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), and Omoyele Sowore of the African Action Congress (AAC). Tinubu, who is seeking a second four-year term, won the 2023 presidential election with 8,794,726 votes. Atiku finished second with 6,984,520 votes, while Obi came third with 6,101,533 votes. Following the 2023 election, both Atiku and Obi challenged Tinubu’s victory, citing alleged electoral irregularities, delays in uploading results, and problems with the Independent National Electoral Commission’s (INEC) result transmission portal. item.title: 2027: APGA adopts Tinubu, says, you don’t change a winning team
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The All Progressives Grand Alliance APGA has presented its flag to President Bola Tinubu as its presidential candidate at the All Progressives Congress APC campaign rally in Awka, Anambra State. APC National Chairman, Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, announced the alliance at the rally held at Alex Ekwueme Square on Thursday. “The chairman of PDP is not here, but he is well in his spirit. The chairman of Accord is here. We are four in one. Four political parties supporting one candidate. President Bola Ahmed Tinubu,” he said. Yilwatda then invited Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, to present the APGA flag, with Vice President Kashim Shettima receiving it on Tinubu’s behalf. Soludo said the handover made the rally unlike any other. He said it was the first time APGA was presenting its flag to the Tinubu/Shettima ticket as its presidential candidate. He also reminded the crowd that Anambra was where the ticket did worst in 2023. According to him, it recorded 5,111 votes, or 0.8 per cent. “Ndi Anambra, are we going to do far better than 2023? We will not be there again,” he said. The governor said Ndigbo would lose from another round of political isolation. “Let us make this campaign a conversation, not an argument among ourselves. In a democracy, what leverage do we have other than our votes and having alliance with the rest of the country?There is work to be done, but you don’t change a winning team”, he said. Soludo said power would move to the North in 2031 and that the South should first complete its eight years. He also said the contest was already decided. “This election, to the best of my knowledge, is already won and lost. No candidate before 2023 presented a better manifesto, better agenda for Nigeria. And so far, less than two months to go, no candidate has presented a credible alternative,” he said. Yilwatda said the President had shown confidence in the Southeast by giving its sons key roles. He named the Minister of Works, Senator David Umahi, who he said is constructimg good roads. He said even the opposition used those roads. “Even Peter Obi is using our roads. Atiku is using our roads. Those roads are constructed by your son, Umahi,” he said. Yilwatda described Tinubu as the most experienced and formidable of the candidates, pointing to his record as Lagos State governor and at the centre. He said the President had stabilised the economy and fixed roads, power and education. item.title: Man accused of AI-assisted exam cheating found dead in Seoul
item.description: A South Korean man suspected of using artificial intelligence (AI) to obtain a perfect score in the country’s law school entrance examination has been found dead at a motel in Seoul. Lee Jin-woo was discovered at a motel in Cheonho-dong, Gangdong District, eastern Seoul, at about 1:12 p.m. on Thursday, emergency authorities said. According to Yonhap News TV, a note was also found at the scene, reportedly indicating that Lee was physically and mentally exhausted. However, the note reportedly contained no admission of cheating or explanation of the allegations against him. Authorities said they would examine the scene to establish the circumstances surrounding his death. Lee had attracted public attention over allegations that he used AI to cheat in the Legal Education Eligibility Test (LEET), the examination required for admission into law schools in South Korea. In an attempt to dispel the suspicions, he had announced plans to answer questions from the Korean language section of the 2027 College Scholastic Ability Test in real time on Thursday morning. However, he failed to appear at the designated venue by 8:40 a.m., when the examination began. Police launched a search after receiving a report at about 8:42 a.m. expressing concern over his whereabouts. According to the police, Lee left his home on Wednesday and travelled to a lodging facility in Gwangjin District, eastern Seoul, before leaving on Thursday morning. He reportedly took a taxi towards Songpa District, southern Seoul, between 8 a.m. and 9 a.m., before heading to Gangdong District, where his body was later discovered. Lee had previously gained attention after revealing that he had scored between the sixth and eighth tiers in previous college entrance examinations, which use a nine-tier grading system, with higher numbers representing lower scores. He said he later developed a better understanding of studying and reading comprehension, eventually gaining admission into Korea University’s Department of Political Science and International Relations in 2024 and Seoul National University’s School of Dentistry in 2026. He also reportedly achieved a perfect score in the LEET while attending Seoul National University. However, his academic achievements came under scrutiny following allegations of AI-assisted cheating in a national tax accountant certification examination. Questions were subsequently raised over whether he had also used AI to cheat in the LEET and the college entrance examinations for the 2024 and 2026 academic years. The Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency said on Wednesday that it had assigned a criminal complaint against Lee, bordering on allegations of obstruction of business, obstruction of official duties and fraud, to its Provincial Special Detective Corps. Following his death, police are expected to close the case without prosecution, as criminal proceedings cannot continue against a deceased suspect. item.title: Fountain of Life Church postpones 2026 Thanksgiving service
item.description: The Fountain of Life Church has postponed its 2026 Thanksgiving service, earlier scheduled for Sunday, November 22, amid an ongoing leadership crisis involving Senior Pastor Jimmy Odukoya and members of its Board of Trustees. The Lagos-based church announced the postponement in a notice shared on its official social media platforms on Thursday, November 19. The notice read, “Please be informed that our Thanksgiving 2026 Service, previously scheduled for Sunday, November 22, has been postponed. A new date will be communicated in due course.” The church did not give any reason for the decision or indicate when the service would be rescheduled. The development comes amid a leadership dispute following an announcement by some members of the Board of Trustees withdrawing recognition of Odukoya as the church’s senior pastor with immediate effect. The trustees reportedly based their decision on a review of the church’s constitution and a December 2021 video recording in which the late founder, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, outlined succession arrangements that identified another individual as his preferred successor, while assigning Jimmy Odukoya administrative and youth church responsibilities. They also cited governance concerns and issues surrounding Odukoya’s recent remarriage. However, Odukoya and representatives of the church rejected the announcement, describing it as constitutionally invalid and not a decision properly taken by the Board of Trustees. They maintained that he remains the duly appointed senior pastor and chairman of the board, following his unanimous approval for the positions in September 2023 after his father’s death. The trustees subsequently reaffirmed their position and appointed Pastor Rotimi Okpaise to provide interim spiritual and administrative leadership pending further consultations. The crisis has also extended to the control of the church’s official social media accounts, with both sides reportedly disputing authority over the platforms. Odukoya was notably absent from the church’s midweek service on Thursday as the leadership dispute continued. The Thanksgiving service had attracted attention amid the unfolding crisis, with the postponement adding another development to the dispute over the church’s leadership and administration. item.title: Road crashes fall 13.8%, deaths drop to 941 in Q3 2026 — FRSC
item.description: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja The Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) has reported a 13.8 per cent reduction in road traffic crashes across Nigeria in the third quarter of 2026, with fatalities dropping from 1,077 in the corresponding period of 2025 to 941. The Corps also recorded a decline in the number of people injured, from 6,856 to 5,864, representing a 14.5 per cent reduction. The figures were disclosed in a statement on Thursday by the Corps Public Education Officer, Osondu Ohaeri, following the end-of-year strategy session with commanding officers at the FRSC headquarters in Abuja. According to the statement, 2,098 road traffic crashes were recorded between July and September 2026, compared with 2,434 in the corresponding period of 2025. The reduction of 336 crashes exceeded the Corps’ 10 per cent reduction target. Similarly, the number of people injured dropped by 992, while fatalities declined by 136, representing a 12.6 per cent reduction. The statement said, “A comparative assessment of the two periods shows that road traffic crashes declined from 2,434 in Q3 2025 to 2,098 in Q3 2026, representing 336 fewer crashes. “Road traffic injuries also dropped significantly from 6,856 to 5,864, a reduction of 992, while recorded fatalities decreased from 1,077 to 941, representing 136 fewer deaths.” The Corps attributed the improvement to enhanced patrol operations, crash prevention measures, public education and enforcement of traffic laws. Ahead of the 2026 festive season, the Corps Marshal, Shehu Mohammed, directed commanding officers nationwide to intensify patrol operations along high-risk routes, improve traffic management and strengthen collaboration with other security and emergency response agencies. He also ordered the strategic deployment of ambulances, rescue teams and tow trucks, while directing commands to sustain public awareness campaigns on safe driving. “As the nation approaches the 2026 festive season, the Corps Marshal has directed Commanding Officers across the country to translate the gains recorded into more effective highway operations, with particular attention to strategic patrol deployment along high-risk corridors, improved traffic management, stronger collaboration with sister agencies, strategic positioning of ambulances, rescue teams and tow trucks, and sustained public enlightenment,” the statement added. Mohammed also urged commanding officers to strengthen supervision, prioritise personnel welfare and enforce discipline, warning that the Corps would maintain zero tolerance for extortion, negligence and abuse of authority. In his remarks, the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, George Akume, said the figures reflected progress made under the reforms introduced by the Corps Marshal, particularly the increased emphasis on technology and operational intelligence. item.title: Africa Records 71.4bn Transactions, $1.8trn Instant Payments In 2025 — Report
item.description: Africa’s instant payment systems processed 71.4 billion transactions worth $1.8 trillion in 2025, nearly three times the volume recorded in 2021, according to a new report by the AfricaNenda Foundation, the United Nations Economic Commission for Africa and the World Bank Group. The fifth edition of the State of Inclusive Instant Payment Systems in Africa (SIIPS) report, published on Thursday, highlighted the rapid expansion of digital payment infrastructure across the continent but warns that access alone has not translated into widespread everyday usage. According to the report, 89 per cent of African adults live in countries with access to an instant payment system. However, a survey of 1,403 digital payment users across 15 markets found that 55 per cent still use cash for about half of their transactions. It also found that more than half of respondents had experienced payment problems, including delays and transfers to the wrong recipients, while one in three affected users never reported such incidents, largely because they did not know how to do so. “Five years ago, our first report mapped 29 instant payment systems; today there are 39, and one in two African adults live in a country served by an inclusive instant payment system IIPS,” said Sabine F. Mensah, who is Deputy CEO of AfricaNenda Foundation and lead author of the report. “The question has changed. It is no longer whether Africans can pay instantly, but whether they trust the system enough to stop reaching for cash. Our research shows that trust is won in seconds, through a payment that goes through instantly, with preventive safeguards such as recipient name validation, and a payment confirmation message received in real time. It is kept by getting timely resolution and people’s money back when something goes wrong.” (L-R): Deputy CEO AfricaNenda Foundation, Sabine Mensah; CEO AfricaNenda Foundation, Robert Ochola; and Deputy CEO AfricaNenda Foundation, Akinwale Goodluck, at the report launch on Thursday, November 19, 2026. 39 Instant Payment Systems The report identified 39 live instant payment systems across Africa, comprising 35 domestic systems in 29 countries and four regional systems. Overall, 43 African countries now have access to instant payment capabilities through domestic or regional platforms. Four domestic systems were introduced in the past year in Liberia, Burundi, Guinea and Mauritania, while a new regional system now serves the eight countries of the West African Economic and Monetary Union (WAEMU). Another 17 countries have instant payment system projects underway. Transaction volumes, according to the report, have grown by an average of 28 per cent annually since 2021, while the average transaction value has declined from $45 to $26, indicating increased use for smaller, everyday purchases. item.title: 2027: No rainbow coalition in Ebonyi, APC insists
item.description: By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki The All Progressives Congress (APC) in Ebonyi State has dismissed suggestions of a rainbow coalition ahead of the 2027 general elections, insisting that Governor Francis Nwifuru deserves a second term based on his administration’s achievements. The spokesman of the APC Divine Mandate Campaign Council in the state, Senator Emmanuel Onwe, stated this on Thursday during the inaugural press briefing of the campaign organisation at the party’s secretariat in Abakaliki. Onwe, a former Commissioner for Information, also announced that the APC would flag off its governorship campaign on November 26, 2026, in Afikpo Local Government Area of the state. He said the party would focus on showcasing the achievements of the Nwifuru administration rather than engaging in activities capable of undermining the democratic rights of opposition parties. Onwe also dissociated the APC from the alleged removal or destruction of campaign posters and billboards belonging to opposition parties, declaring that the ruling party neither condoned political violence nor supported lawlessness ahead of the elections. Responding to questions from journalists on allegations of the destruction of opposition campaign materials, including an incident reportedly involving some political supporters, he maintained that the party had no policy or directive authorising such acts. “It is not possible for a ruling government to have a policy of destruction, whether it is the destruction of posters, billboards or the commission of violence against the opposition. No. “APC doesn’t support destruction of opposition posters and billboards. I charge the police to arrest anybody destroying opposition posters,” he said. He added that the APC in Ebonyi would pursue its political engagements through legitimate and issue-based campaigns. “APC in Ebonyi State will campaign with integrity, with honour, and will only project the positive achievements of the APC government in Ebonyi State. No more, no less,” he said. The campaign spokesman advised individuals and political parties aggrieved by the alleged destruction of their campaign materials to seek redress through the appropriate security agencies rather than resorting to self-help. “I would advise those who feel aggrieved in any shape, in any way, in any form, to take the matter to the police,” he stated. Onwe further assured that neither the state government, the APC State Working Committee nor any party official would shield anyone found culpable of unlawful conduct, irrespective of political affiliation. He said the campaign organisation was committed to democratic competition through constructive political discourse and the presentation of the administration’s record in governance. item.title: Igbo presidency must be eight full years — Oshiomhole
item.description: Senator Adams Oshiomhole has declared that any Nigerian president of Igbo extraction must serve a full eight-year tenure, insisting that the South-East should not settle for a truncated presidential term. Oshiomhole stated this on Thursday at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Anambra State, where he also praised Governor Chukwuma Soludo’s administration and President Bola Tinubu’s policies on education and university funding. “When Ndi Igbo will become president, it must be eight full years. No half cup. It will be full cup by those with brain, with courage, and fill the gaps,” the former Edo State governor said. He described Anambra as “the headquarters of intellectuals”, citing the state’s contributions to Nigeria’s intellectual and political development, including the emergence of the country’s first President, Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe. “Historically, it has been so. You produce the Zik of Africa, not just Zik of Nigeria,” he said. Reflecting on his childhood in a village without a hospital or school, Oshiomhole praised Tinubu’s education initiatives, particularly the provision of financial assistance and loans to students. He recalled travelling several kilometres to attend primary school, saying his personal experience made him appreciate policies aimed at ensuring that disadvantaged Nigerians had access to education. “When I find a president who remembers people of my background, and say you shall not lack education; I will give you money. I will give you loan, which you can only pay when you get job,” he said. The senator also commended the Federal Government’s handling of issues affecting universities, particularly the maintenance of academic calendars and improved remuneration for lecturers. He claimed that Nigerian universities had experienced four years without strikes, arguing that the stability of academic calendars was important to maintaining the credibility of public universities. “Now, for four years, there has been no strike. This is a threat to those who live on primary ownership of a public university, because the only reason people say they are children there is because of the integrity of academic calendar,” he said. Oshiomhole attributed previous disruptions in the university system to what he described as poor leadership, saying inadequate remuneration had contributed to the departure of experienced academics from universities. He said Tinubu was addressing the challenges through improved remuneration and efforts to attract experienced academics back into the university system. “President Bola Tinubu is not only respecting that calendar by dealing with issues confronting us, but also ensuring that by proper remuneration, we bring back to academia the finest brains in our society,” he said. He urged Anambra residents to support the President, expressing confidence in the benefits of the Federal Government’s education initiatives. item.title: Soludo presents APGA flag to Tinubu as 2027 flagbearer
item.description: By Vincent Ujumadu Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, has formally presented the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) flag to President Bola Tinubu, declaring the party’s support for his re-election bid in the 2027 general election. The symbolic presentation took place at Alex Ekwueme Square, Awka, during the “SoluTinubu 2027” mega rally, where Vice President Kashim Shettima received the flag on behalf of Tinubu. Addressing party members and political leaders at the rally, Soludo said the gesture represented an effort to integrate the South-East into mainstream national politics. “We are representing APGA, and we are presenting our own party flag to the President,” the governor said. He urged Anambra residents to reconsider their voting pattern in the 2027 presidential election, recalling that Tinubu secured only 0.8 per cent of the votes cast in the state in the 2023 presidential election, compared with the 73 per cent mandate Soludo secured during his second-term governorship election. Soludo said the rally followed weeks of statewide town hall engagements organised by his party, which he described as conversations centred on the collective survival and prosperity of the Igbo people. Acknowledging existing grievances and political sentiments in the South-East, he argued that the region could not afford to remain politically isolated. “In a democracy, what leverage do we have other than our votes and alliance with the whole country? What do we gain by wasting our votes again?” he asked. He argued that supporting a Southern president to complete an eight-year tenure before power rotates to the North would provide the South-East with greater political leverage and opportunities to secure federal infrastructure projects and address regional security concerns. The governor also expressed confidence in the Tinubu-Shettima ticket, claiming that the administration’s economic and development agenda had not been matched by a credible opposition alternative. He urged the people of the South-East to support the President’s re-election bid, describing the political alignment as an opportunity for the region to strengthen its participation in national affairs. Receiving the flag on Tinubu’s behalf, Shettima commended the people of Anambra for their turnout and assured the state and the wider South-East of the Federal Government’s commitment to fulfilling its campaign promises if re-elected. The rally also attracted several political leaders, including Imo State Governor, Hope Uzodimma; Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Benjamin Kalu; Minister of Works, Dave Umahi; former Anambra State Governor, Chris Ngige; and Senator Adams Oshiomhole. The leaders urged grassroots mobilisers to canvass support for Tinubu across party lines and at polling units, stressing the need for greater political integration of the South-East into national politics. item.title: State health budgets rise 67% to ₦3.3tn — Pate
item.description: By Edwin Philip, Lafia Combined health budgets of state governments across Nigeria have increased by more than 67 per cent, from ₦1.97 trillion in 2023 to over ₦3.3 trillion in 2026, while national health insurance enrolment has risen by 50 per cent, from 16 million to nearly 24 million people within the same period. The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Muhammad Ali Pate, disclosed this on Thursday at the opening of the 67th National Council on Health (NCH) in Lafia, Nasarawa State, with the theme, “From Commitments to Results.” Pate said Nigeria had fulfilled 41 presidential health sector commitments and recorded improvements in 12 of 13 core national health indicators since the launch of the Nigeria Health Sector Renewal Investment Initiative in December 2023. Highlighting progress in healthcare delivery and financial protection, the minister said skilled birth deliveries in health facilities supported by the Basic Health Care Provision Fund (BHCPF) increased from 4.8 million in 2023 to nearly eight million by mid-2026. He added that fourth antenatal care visits also rose from six million to 8.7 million within the period. According to him, emergency transport systems have conveyed more than 100,000 women and newborns to healthcare facilities, while the Federal Government’s free emergency obstetric care initiative has funded more than 80,000 caesarean sections. He said over 50,000 patients had also accessed free 48-hour emergency care across 507 empanelled facilities, while more than 5,000 patients benefited from dialysis subsidies of up to 80 per cent. On healthcare workforce development, Pate said the proportion of health facilities with at least two midwives or community health workers had increased from 12 per cent to nearly 91 per cent nationally. He said nearly 20,000 skilled birth attendants had been recruited across 22 states, alongside almost 5,000 community health workers in 10 states, while close to 80,000 frontline health workers had undergone retraining. On immunisation, the minister said vaccination campaigns had reached more than 100 million children aged zero to nine with measles and rubella vaccines, while over 70 million adolescent girls had received the Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine against cervical cancer. He further disclosed that 10 domestic health manufacturing factories and production lines were now producing medicines, rapid diagnostic test kits, mosquito nets and medical oxygen, with six commissioned in 2026 alone. He said the development was supported by more than ₦24 billion in tax waivers granted under President Bola Tinubu’s June 2024 Executive Order. Despite the progress, Pate warned that Nigerian households continued to bear a disproportionate share of healthcare costs through out-of-pocket payments. item.title: [VIDEO] Drama As Ngige Urges Residents To Vote For APC ‘From Top To Bottom’ At Anambra Presidential Rally
item.description: There was a mild drama at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Anambra State on Thursday when a former governor of the state, Chris Ngige, urged residents to vote for the APC in the 2027 presidential, National Assembly, and House of Assembly elections. The former Minister of Labour and Employment, who spoke in Igbo, said Anambra residents had one target. “We will vote for the APC from top to bottom,” Ngige said, prompting reactions from participants at the rally, including Governor Charles Soludo of the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA), who stood beside him on stage and told his predecessor that the rally is a joint one. The former governor, who said he was not surprised by the reactions, later told members of APGA to vote for candidates of their choice. “Okay, members of APGA — freedom of choice — when you get to the polling booth, vote for the better place,” he said. Ngige added that while people were free to choose between APGA and the APC, Anambra desires to be connected to the Federal Government at the centre and get it through the ruling party. Earlier, the former minister said he remains a member of the APC, claiming that he brought the party to the South-East. “I am still a member of the APC, bona fide member, because I brought APC to the South East — 2013/2014,” he said. “The only thing is that I told people I am on sabbatical, but even if I am on sabbatical, my governor cannot be doing something, and the Vice President is coming physically, and the governor has called me to say we are here, and I would say I won’t come. No.” Ngige said people should not be forced but persuaded to vote during the 2027 general election. He also said those stopping people from campaigning are not doing so in the name of the APC. “We don’t want that — destruction of vehicles, stoning of people. No! We don’t want that. We must emulate other people practising democracy,” the former Anambra governor said. “Democracy gives you the right of choice; even inside the same family, you must exercise that.” Watch Ngige’s remarks in the video below. ﻿ The post [VIDEO] Drama As Ngige Urges Residents To Vote For APC ‘From Top To Bottom’ At Anambra Presidential Rally appeared first on Channels Television .
